messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — INC-20260315-01
incident-bot: high p99 latency observed for dedicated-eu7 pool (streaming tails). p95 jumped from ~380ms to ~1.6s, p99 ~2.9s. queue_depth trending up: 420 -> 1,123. autoscaler attempted scale but warmup/handshake failures seen. paging @sara_ops (oncall). metrics: https://metrics.redwood.example/d/ops/pool-eu7?from=now-30m, runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.example/dedicated-warmup

Sara (sara_ops): grabbing this — thanks. I can confirm p95/p99 jump and large accumulation in hotshot queue. Streaming stalls visible in trace: many requests waiting for KV warmup. going to mute low-priority routes and mark routing policy to fallback-tier. Will post timeline + actions.

Sara (sara_ops): initial quick triage: autoscaler requested +6 slots at 1768799940, but handshake/warmup logs show repeated timeouts (handshake err: "HandshakeTimeout", warmup: "kv-load-failed"). suspects: image pull delays on new nodes + slow kv warmup path for this model variant.

mike_sre: looking. autoscaler logs --> control-plane queue backpressure, rate limit on provisioning API. see snippet:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:23Z autoscaler: request_scale(pool=eu7-dedicated, delta=6)
2026-03-15T09:12:30Z provisioner: create_node -> Pending (ImagePullBackOff)
2026-03-15T09:13:02Z runtime: handshake timeout after 30s -> warmup aborted
```
I can run a manual `redwoodctl pools scale` to force-add existing spare nodes if infra approves.

anya_eng: adding context from model side: the model variant serving eu7 includes a.kv prefetch that is heavy on cold-starts. When we scale and workers come up, warmup tries to prime large embeddings (300M) which takes ~20-45s — if handshake window is 30s it will fail and backend flags node as unhealthy. Suggest two mitigations: 1) increase handshake/warmup window to 90s for this pool (temporary), 2) route a % of traffic to a quantized smaller variant while nodes warm. both are low-risk.

jen_prod: customer impact: CS report of slowed streaming in EU region. Sam_CS, pls compile list of customers with sustained errors vs degraded streaming so we can notify. Include note about potential ETA for full recovery.

sam_cs: working on templates. Draft sent to #customers-notify for review: "We're seeing degraded streaming in EU. We're actively mitigating; some requests may see higher latency or reconnects. Next update in 30 min." cc @jen_prod

rick_infra: FYI I see provisioner pods hitting occasional image registry rate limiting from our image host in eu-west-2. Manual workaround: switch to fallback image mirror or pre-pull. I'm going to pre-pull the runtime image onto spare nodes and kick restart of node-provisioner. Commands: `kubectl -n infra get pods | grep provisioner` then `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/provisioner`.

mike_sre: performing manual scale to buy time: `redwoodctl pools scale --pool eu7-dedicated --count +4 --force` (executed). Nodes created but some are Pending due to image pull. Rick, please pre-pull.

rick_infra: pre-pull started. tail from provisioner:
```
[09:18:02] pulling image runtime:v2.3.1 -> 12%
[09:18:37] pulled -> unpacking
[09:19:01] node registered -> ready
[09:19:07] runtime warmup: kv-load start
[09:19:25] runtime warmup: kv-load complete (230ms)
```
progressing.

anya_eng: toggled routing policy to send 30% of streaming traffic to quantized-variant (q2) and deprioritized non-SLA hotshot queue. Command used: `redwoodctl routing update --pool eu7-dedicated --policy fallback:30 --deprioritize:hotshot`. Monitoring now.

Sara (sara_ops): executing temporary increase of handshake timeout to 90s for pool EU7 (as discussed) — applying config change now. This should reduce warmup aborts.

deploy-bot: NOTE: auto-deploys to eu7 currently blocked — nodes cordoned by autoscaler during scale ops.

mike_sre: after manual interventions: p99 reduced from 2.9s -> ~850ms over last 5m, p95 ~420ms. queue depth falling: 1,123 -> 312. Streaming stalls reduced but some traces still show tail stalls for large prompts.

Sara (sara_ops): mitigation steps summary (in-flight):
- manual `redwoodctl` scale +4 nodes (mike)
- pre-pull runtime image and restart provisioner (rick)
- increased handshake/warmup window to 90s (sara)
- route 30% to quantized fallback variant (anya)
- deprioritize non-SLA hotshot queue (anya)
- CS notification drafted and queued (sam)

jen_prod: can we estimate customer-visible outage window so we can push a status page update? current best estimate: partial mitigation within 20-30m, full convergence 60-90m depending on warmup. pls confirm numbers.

mike_sre: agree with estimate. If provisioner keeps pre-pulling images and handshake window holds, we should be stable in ~45-60m. If image registry rate limiting reappears we may need to flip to mirror permanently for the pool.

sam_cs: sent initial notice to impacted customers at 09:22 UTC. will follow up with ETA update at 09:50 UTC.

Sara (sara_ops): formal handoff: I'm going to escalate this to a P1 livepage with oncall rotation extended. Handoff details: incident ID INC-20260315-01, mitigation applied (see above), current state: partial mitigation, monitoring. Owner for postmortem: @mike_sre. Next steps: confirm warmup success across all new nodes, confirm queue depth stable <200, then revert routing and handshake changes gracefully.

mike_sre: assigning postmortem and follow-ups:
- root cause hypothesis: combined image-pull delays + warmup handshake timeout causing autoscaler to mark new nodes unhealthy -> provisioning stalls -> sustained queue/backlog.
- action items: add image mirror for eu7, revisit warmup handshake defaults, add autoscaler backoff wiggle to avoid tight failure loops, create runbook step to pre-pull images on scale events.

rick_infra: marking infra action item: `infra-1234` create mirror + pre-pull cron.

Sara (sara_ops): closing livepage handoff here — monitoring for 2h. If any regressions ping @sara_ops directly or reopen page. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation observed. p99 down to 820ms, p95 410ms; queue depth 312 -> 198 over last 15m. Keep watch for 2h.
